multiApp.method: RSS of the Playwright-managed browser processes. Sequential: one tab visiting three apps (current policy removes the left frame). Kept: one more tab per app keeps every frame alive, so it also counts each tab's portal page and overstates frame-only cost.
multiApp.reading: Switching apps with one live frame costs about 15-25 MiB per visited app and 120-320 ms per open. Keeping frames alive costs about 130-200 MiB (Chromium/Firefox) and 330-470 MiB (WebKit) per extra tab, so removing a left frame (current policy) stays the default for D5.

cookieInterference.ports: a cookie the frame writes is visible to the portal origin (same host)
cookieInterference.hosts: not visible to the portal (separate sites)

observations.keyboard: Tab from the portal reaches the app input inside the frame and Shift+Tab returns to the portal in all three browsers (headless Firefox keeps Tab on the last element when nothing follows the frame)
observations.print: Allowed by the sandbox in every browser: Chromium fires beforeprint, WebKit returns without a dialog, headless Firefox opens a blocking print dialog (that step is skipped in Firefox because the dialog breaks the automation afterwards)

observations.accessibility: The frame carries the app name as its title; screen reader output itself was not inspected
